div.l: Ne leet his sheep a combred in the myre
And ran to londoıı̄un vn to seint poules
To seke hym a chauntry for soules
Or with a bretherhede to ben witholde
But dwelled at home / and kepte wel his folde
So that the wolf ne made it not miscarie
He was a Shepperde and not a mcernarie
And though he holy were and v̉ertuous
He was not to synfull men dispitous
Ne of his speche daungerous ne digne
But in his speche / discreet and benigne
To drawen folke to heuene by fayrnesse
By good ensaumple / this was his besinesse
But it were ony ꝑpersone obstinate
What so he were of lowe or high estate
Hym wolde he snybbe / sharply for þe nones
A better preest I trowe that nowher non is
He wayted after no pompe and reủerence
Ne maked him a spiced conscience
But cristes lore and his apostelis twelue
He taughte / but first he vsed it hym selue
With him ther was a ploughman was his brother
That hadde ylad of dong ful many a fother
A trewe swynker / and a good was he
Lyuynge in pees and ꝑparfite charite
God loued he best with al his herte
At alle tymes / though him gamed or smte
And than his neyghbore / right as him selue
He wolde thresshe / and ther to dyke and delue
For cristes sake for eủery poủere wight
Withoute hire ȝif it lay in his myght
His tythes paied he ful faire and wel
Bothe of his ꝓpropre swynk and his catel
In a tabbard he rode vpon a mere
Ther was also a Reue / and a Mellere
A Sompnoᵘur and a pardoner also
A Maunciple and my self ther were no mo
The Mellere was a stout carle for the nones
Ful big he was of brawn and eke of bones
